papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.authors: Fatima Yatim, Alan Sitkin, Cadenza Academic Translations
papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The analysis highlights the crucial interactions between internal and external dynamics, identifying essential conditions for successful innovations: effective mobilization of internal resources, robust institutional support, and early and active user involvement. However, the study also identifies limitations in citizen engagement, particularly in the evaluation phase of innovations. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.summary: Carbohydrate binding proteins (CBPs) are alluring and challenging targets in biology. CBPs achieve high-affinity interactions with their substrates through multivalent interactions with carbohydrates, often in branched, heterogeneous structures. Many cell recognition events and host-pathogen interactions are mediated by these carbohydrate-protein interactions. Therefore, the development of glycan-based mimics and disruptors of these interactions have applications in studying target CBPs, carbohydrate-based vaccines, immunomodulating agents, diagnostics, and therapeutics against cancer and other diseases. papers.summary: Chopin adhered to traditional practices in musical form to a far greater extent than hitherto acknowledged. He took certain standard formal paths with remarkable consistency throughout his compositional career and across almost all his favoured genres. His choices were grounded in eighteenth-century routines concerning intrathematic functions and schemata. papers.title: Embodied Interaction and Audio-Visuals in Performing Arts
papers.title_ja: 舞台芸術におけるエンボディード・インタラクションとオーディオビジュアル
papers.summary: With the emergence of technologies for collecting data for the body, such as motion tracking and biosignal sensing, there has been an interest in using these technologies in performing arts. In such performance settings, this data has been mapped to different types of output, such as audio-visuals. In this chapter, we discuss the intersection of embodied interaction, performing arts and audio-visual practice. In particular, we will present two lines of work, one exploring audio-visuals in contemporary dance (the Moving Digits project) and another combining gesture, electronic music, and visuals (works by Atau Tanaka). From the analysis of these two lines of work and related projects, we map out the area of embodied interaction in performative audio-visual practice and identify relevant categories.

papers.summary: The Book of Architecture of John Thorpe (c.1565-1655) consists of some 295 drawings ranging primarily from the 1590s to the 1620s and covering 168 buildings, mainly but not only English, and amongst the greatest of the period. The drawings include plans, elevations, some full-size sections of mouldings, and a depiction of the five orders derived from Hans Blum’s 1550 treatise on the orders. Bound in a hard cover in the 18th c., since 1810 the album has been preserved in one of London’s most iconic museums of British architecture, created by the celebrated architect Sir John Soane (1753-1837), who added to the album with about six sketches of his own.
